LESSON: WRITING 7.5.1 COMPOSITION WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.5: Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How would you ensure that you make your composition clear and interesting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the steps in the writing process
2. write a dialogue on a given topic
3. appreciate the importance of the writing process in enhancing clear communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 7.5.1 COMPOSITION WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 7.5.1 COMPOSITION WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the steps in the writing process

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the steps in the writing process. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the steps in the writing process.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the steps in the writing process. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a dialogue on a given topic

What this means
In this part you learn to write a dialogue on a given topic. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a dialogue on a given topic.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a dialogue on a given topic. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of the writing process in enhancing clear communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of the writing process in enhancing clear communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of the writing process in enhancing clear communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of the writing process in enhancing clear communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the steps in the writing process)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing to a partner. (skill: write a dialogue on a given topic)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of the writing process in enhancing clear communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the steps in the writing process.
3. Practise this skill: write a dialogue on a given topic.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of the writing process in enhancing clear communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How would you ensure that you make your composition clear and interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the steps in the writing process.
5. Be able to: write a dialogue on a given topic.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
